_comment: P74 WP4, re-landed P79 WP-C against the finished P79 tree. Every tracked tools/**/*.py and shared/**/*.py must either expose a --selftest that tools/selftest_sweep.py can discover, or appear here with a written reason. This list is the named residue of the coverage work: it exists so the uncovered count cannot grow silently, which is how the OG-extractor defect (P74-0) survived. Adding an entry is a deliberate act that a reviewer can argue with; forgetting to write a selftest is not.
_review: Revisit when a file here gains real logic. 'Runner' and 'package marker' entries are permanent by nature; 'network-bound' entries become testable the day their pure seams are factored out, and that refactor is the right way to close them.

exempt.tools/sync_check.py: The drift guard itself. The battery runs it on every change, so executing it IS its test; a --selftest would be ceremony wrapped around the thing already under test.
exempt.tools/handoff_sim.py: A 10-phase / 38-check end-to-end runner. Wiring it into the sweep is tracked separately (PRE-3) because its write phases need their sandbox redirect reviewed before it runs unattended.
exempt.tools/geo_e2e_proof.py: Itself an end-to-end proof runner (17 checks) executed in the battery.
exempt.tools/count_truth.py: A runner whose entire output is the assertion; the battery runs it and invariant 48 checks its numbers against live docs.
exempt.tools/version.py: A runner: `version.py --check` is the assertion, and CI runs it.
exempt.tools/registry_io.py: A 62-line single-writer shim. Its behaviour is asserted by source_currency's selftest (29 checks) and by drift invariants 42 and 56, which is closer coverage than a self-test of two functions.
exempt.tools/new_skill.py: A scaffolder whose output is validated by the drift guard the moment a skill is created.
exempt.tools/update.py: A runner; its logic is covered by update_check.py, which has its own selftest.
exempt.tools/sync_cache.py: A runner over the cache index; exercised by the cache build path and the setup flow.
exempt.shared/connectors/connectors.py: Executed on every drift-guard run by invariant 53, which imports the resolver and calls resolve({}) over the committed registry. That is stronger than a selftest because it runs against real data.
exempt.shared/cache/cache.py: Exercised by mcp_server's selftest (synthetic index), keyword_offline and setup. A direct selftest would need to build a temp SQLite index; worth doing, but it must never run against the real index.local.db, so it is deliberately deferred rather than rushed.
exempt.tools/acquire.py: Every entry point performs network or browser I/O. Its pure seams (_links, _same_domain) are small; the honest close is to factor them into a helper module with its own selftest rather than pretend a network tool is offline-testable.
exempt.tools/fetch_resilient.py: All four prongs perform real network requests; only _robots_ok has a pure short-circuit. Same close as acquire.py.
exempt.tools/fetch_cache.py: A single _root() path helper with no branching logic.
exempt.tools/videoedit/resolve.py: A stub surface: its functions raise NotImplementedError pending the Resolve integration, so there is no behaviour to assert yet.
exempt.tools/publishing/__init__.py: Exercised by the sweep's package entry, `python -m publishing --selftest`.
exempt.tools/publishing/_http.py: Covered by the same package entry; its callers are the four platform clients, each of which has a selftest.
exempt.tools/videoedit/__init__.py: Package marker and re-export shim; no independent logic.
exempt.shared/docintel/wer.py: A pure word-error-rate helper fully exercised by coverage_verify's selftest (19 checks), which is its only caller.
exempt.shared/docintel/classify.py: Exercised by handoff/inbox.py, whose own selftest drives classification end to end.
